attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A present-state compound observation. 'For the taking' is fairly rendered as freely available. 'Here to stay' is correctly not treated as a dated forecast.

contract.note: The result turns on how 'dark web' and 'replicate' are read, and the speaker defined neither. Reading dark web as hidden services is literal but defensible. The contract avoids penalising him: public-torrent availability does not count as contradiction.

evidence.note: Dated 13 Mar 2023. Shows cheap fine-tuning with a published recipe. Does not show easy pretraining from scratch.
Reputable report that verified LLaMA weights leaked via a 4chan torrent on 3 Mar 2023. Supports unofficial availability, not dark-web hidden services.
April 2022 open model release, outside the target period. Background on how the recipe spread.

reviews.rationale: Part of the claim is supported: practical fine-tuning recipes and unofficial availability of leaked weights. Easy replication of base models and dark-web availability are not established, and nothing contradicts any part. The support condition is not fully met and the contradiction condition is not met, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own Atlantic article and endorses it, so these are his words.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' forecast with no deadline. Reading the contest as being about AI misinformation matches the context.

contract.note: Plain reading (repeated adaptation, persistent difficulty) is ordinary and fair. Early resolution is allowed only for contradiction, by a durable end to the contest.

evidence.note: 2024 research on breaking watermarks. Concerns detection of generated text, not misinformation outcomes.
2024 research showing watermarks survive paraphrasing. Not a durable solution, so it does not contradict.
OpenAI's account of its own enforcement, dated Oct 2026 and before the cutoff. Shows continued AI-assisted influence operations and bans. Partial at most, and not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline and no conclusive event ended the contest. Continued adaptation in 2024 to 2026 fits the prediction, but finite examples cannot settle an open-ended forecast. Nothing establishes a durable resolution, so the forecast is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Isolates the claim about the state of knowledge. The 'only solution' clause is opinion and correctly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'a long way' as substantial unresolved foundational problems is an ordinary, fair plain reading.

evidence.note: Dated 8 Mar 2023. Anthropic says of the whole field, not of itself, that no one knew how to make powerful systems robustly behave well.
OpenAI disclosure of 14 Mar 2023. Reports better safety against its own policies but says jailbreaks remain. Not consensus-value alignment.

reviews.rationale: Records from the time show reliable alignment of powerful systems was unsolved. Even the GPT-4 disclosure admits jailbreaks remain. No validated general method for implementing broadly shared human values existed by 14 Mar 2023, which meets the support condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A compound observation. The second clause is loose and near-rhetorical: 'most people' covers an unclear group and no behaviour is defined.

contract.note: 'A lot' as a substantial share is fair. The second clause depends on which population is meant and how behaviour is measured, and the speaker gave neither. The contract keeps the possible groups separate.

evidence.note: The original 2022 survey: 48% gave at least a 10% chance of an extremely bad outcome. Supports substantial concern despite a 17% response rate.
Monmouth poll of US adults, early 2023. Covers attitudes and policy views, not behaviour, and may not be the group Marcus meant.

reviews.rationale: The first clause holds: the survey shows substantial researcher concern. No representative evidence measures whether most people behaved as if unconcerned, and the poll covers attitudes rather than behaviour. The compound claim is not settled, so it is unresolved.
